claim: Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum spring 2026 blockbuster 'Metamorphoses' runs 6 February to 25 May 2026, presenting 80+ masterpieces by Titian, Caravaggio and Rodin around Ovid's poem.
quote: The Rijksmuseum presents its major spring exhibition 'Metamorphoses', inspired by Ovid's famous poem... With more than 80 masterpieces by artists such as Titian, Caravaggio, and Rodin... from 6 February to 25 May 2026.

claim: Madrid's Prado headlines 2026 with 'Prado. 21st Century' (9 June–27 September 2026), surveying 25 years of works acquired by the museum.
quote: "Prado. 21st Century" runs from June 9 to September 27, 2026, offering a journey through the transformation of the Madrid museum over the past quarter of a century.

claim: Madrid's Reina Sofia stages the largest-ever Maruja Mallo retrospective (from 8 October 2025 to 16 March 2026), gathering 90 works by the avant-garde artist.
quote: From October 8 to March 16, 2026, the Reina Sofía Museum hosts the largest retrospective to date on avant-garde artist Maruja Mallo, bringing together 90 works including paintings, drawings, writings, documents and videos.

claim: Rome's Scuderie del Quirinale runs 'Treasures of the Pharaohs', Italy's largest ancient-Egypt show with 130 artifacts loaned from Cairo and Luxor, extended until 14 June 2026.
quote: The exhibition has been extended and will remain open to the public until Sunday, June 14, 2026. In the first ninety days of opening, 250,000 tickets were issued.

claim: Florence's Palazzo Strozzi presents 'Rothko in Florence' (14 March–23 August 2026), a major Mark Rothko show with many works never before seen in Italy.
quote: From March 14 to August 23, 2026, Palazzo Strozzi will host a major exhibition dedicated to Mark Rothko... Curated by Christopher Rothko and Elena Geuna, Rothko in Florence is a unique project conceived specifically for Palazzo Strozzi.

claim: Berlin's Neue Nationalgalerie shows a Constantin Brancusi retrospective (until 9 August 2026), the first major Brancusi exhibition in Germany in over 50 years, co-organised with the Centre Pompidou.
quote: Until 9 August 2026, the museum presents a comprehensive retrospective on Constantin Brancusi, a pioneer of modern sculpture. In cooperation with the Centre Pompidou in Paris... the first major exhibition of this exceptional artist in Germany in over 50 years.

claim: Vienna's Albertina marks its 250th anniversary in 2026 with 'Collecting for the Future' (19 June–11 October 2026), reuniting the collection's founding masterpieces including Duerer's Young Hare.
quote: Collecting for the Future: celebrating 250 years of the Albertina with an exhibition that explores the origins of the collection and how many of the great works became part of it, including Dürer's Young Hare (June 19th to October 11th, 2026).

claim: Basel's Fondation Beyeler devotes its first-ever full exhibition to Paul Cezanne (25 January–25 May 2026), with around 80 oil paintings and watercolours focused on his late career.
quote: A major monographic exhibition dedicated to Paul Cézanne runs from 25 January to 25 May 2026. For the first time in its history, the Fondation Beyeler devotes a full exhibition to Cézanne... around 80 oil paintings and watercolours.

claim: Barcelona's MNAC closes 2026 with 'The Atomic Age', a roughly 250-work show on how the nuclear era reshaped culture, featuring Dali, Duchamp, Yoko Ono and Hilma af Klint.
quote: The major exhibition at MNAC opening at the end of 2026 is "The Atomic Age," which explores how the atomic era has transformed our perception of time, science, politics, and life on Earth through nearly 250 works by artists such as Salvador Dalí, Marcel Duchamp, Yoko Ono, Hilma af Klint, and Nancy Spero.

claim: Brussels' Bozar headlines 2026 with 'Bellezza e Bruttezza' (20 February–14 June 2026), a Renaissance show on beauty versus ugliness with works by Botticelli, Titian and Cranach the Elder.
quote: Dates: February 20 – June 14, 2026. Venue: BOZAR/Centre for Fine Arts... explores "Beauty and Ugliness in the Renaissance"... works by masters including Botticelli, Titian, and Cranach the Elder.

claim: Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum stages a 2026 Canaletto and Bernardo Bellotto cityscapes show, pairing the two vedute painters' depictions of Venice, London and Vienna.
quote: The Kunsthistorisches Museum is showcasing cityscapes by the painters Canaletto and Bernardo Bellotto... presenting their works side by side to illustrate how they saw and painted the same places differently.
